Mini-IPIP: Items and real responses

Source: R/data.R
mini_ipip.Rd

The 20 items of the Mini-IPIP (Donnellan et al., 2006), four per Big Five trait, and the answers of 20,000 people drawn at random from the Open-Source Psychometrics Project's IPIP Big-Five Factor Markers data (1,015,342 respondents, 2016 to 2018). The Mini-IPIP items are part of the 50 IPIP Big-Five markers, so these people answered them among the other 30 items. The items are public domain. Its fit problems and weak scale make it a test case for the pretest (see sc_builtin_instrument()).

Usage

mini_ipip_items

mini_ipip_real

Format

mini_ipip_items: A data frame with 20 rows and 6 columns: item, scale (E, A, C, N or I), scale_label, statement, reverse (11 items are reverse-keyed) and issue.

mini_ipip_real: A data frame with 20,000 rows and 21 columns: country (two-letter code from the respondent's network address, or NA; the largest groups are US (9,918), GB (1,377) and CA (1,269)) and the 20 items. The sample holds only people who answered all 20 items and were the only record from their network address.

An object of class data.frame with 20 rows and 6 columns.

An object of class data.frame with 20000 rows and 21 columns.

Source

Open-Source Psychometrics Project, https://openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/ (IPIP-FFM data, November 2018). The project gives no formal licence for the data. The items are from the International Personality Item Pool (public domain), https://ipip.ori.org. The script is data-raw/instruments.R in the package's GitHub repository.

Details

Known problems. A five-factor model with simple structure fits poorly unless residuals are allowed to correlate, the Intellect/Imagination scale is often the least reliable and mixes imagination with interest in abstract ideas, and the reverse-keyed items share a method factor (Donnellan et al., 2006; Cooper et al., 2010; Baldasaro et al., 2013). The issue column of mini_ipip_items gives a one-line note per item.

Answers are on a 5-point scale (1 = disagree, 3 = neutral, 5 = agree) and are stored as given: Reverse-keyed items are not reversed. Use mini_ipip_items$reverse and 6 - x before scoring. The trait the items measure is Neuroticism (high is less stable), as in the Mini-IPIP. The item names are those of the IPIP Big-Five markers data (EXT, AGR, CSN, EST and OPN with a number), so the full file can be used too.

References

Baldasaro, R. E., Shanahan, M. J., & Bauer, D. J. (2013). Psychometric properties of the Mini-IPIP in a large, nationally representative sample of young adults. Journal of Personality Assessment, 95(1), 74-84. doi:10.1080/00223891.2012.700466

Cooper, A. J., Smillie, L. D., & Corr, P. J. (2010). A confirmatory factor analysis of the Mini-IPIP five-factor model personality scale. Personality and Individual Differences, 48(5), 688-691. doi:10.1016/j.paid.2010.01.004

Donnellan, M. B., Oswald, F. L., Baird, B. M., & Lucas, R. E. (2006). The Mini-IPIP scales: Tiny-yet-effective measures of the Big Five factors of personality. Psychological Assessment, 18(2), 192-203. doi:10.1037/1040-3590.18.2.192

See also

sc_builtin_instrument(), rses_items, dass_items

Examples

mini_ipip_items[, c("item", "scale", "reverse", "statement")]
#>    item scale reverse                                                statement
#> 1  EXT1     E   FALSE                              I am the life of the party.
#> 2  EXT7     E   FALSE          I talk to a lot of different people at parties.
#> 3  EXT2     E    TRUE                                      I don't talk a lot.
#> 4  EXT4     E    TRUE                                I keep in the background.
#> 5  AGR4     A   FALSE                      I sympathize with others' feelings.
#> 6  AGR9     A   FALSE                                 I feel others' emotions.
#> 7  AGR5     A    TRUE          I am not interested in other people's problems.
#> 8  AGR7     A    TRUE                    I am not really interested in others.
#> 9  CSN5     C   FALSE                            I get chores done right away.
#> 10 CSN7     C   FALSE                                            I like order.
#> 11 CSN6     C    TRUE I often forget to put things back in their proper place.
#> 12 CSN4     C    TRUE                                 I make a mess of things.
#> 13 EST8     N   FALSE                             I have frequent mood swings.
#> 14 EST6     N   FALSE                                      I get upset easily.
#> 15 EST2     N    TRUE                           I am relaxed most of the time.
#> 16 EST4     N    TRUE                                      I seldom feel blue.
#> 17 OPN3     I   FALSE                              I have a vivid imagination.
#> 18 OPN4     I    TRUE                   I am not interested in abstract ideas.
#> 19 OPN2     I    TRUE          I have difficulty understanding abstract ideas.
#> 20 OPN6     I    TRUE                        I do not have a good imagination.
